q: Write what happens at the quark level in the beta minus decay of a neutron, and name the mediator particle.
a: One $d$ quark of the neutron turns into a $u$ quark: $d \to u + W^-$, and the $W^-$ boson turns into an electron and an antineutrino, $W^- \to e^- + \bar{\nu}_e$. The neutron $udd$ becomes a proton $uud$. The mediator $W^-$ belongs to the weak interaction.

q: Is the reaction $p + n \to p + p + e^-$ possible? Justify using the conservation laws.
a: It is not. The charge is conserved ($1 + 0 = 1 + 1 - 1$) and the baryon number is conserved ($1 + 1 = 1 + 1 + 0$), but the lepton number is not: at the start $L = 0$, at the end the electron has $L = 1$.
